limitations: The repository is read-only and the requested feature is not implemented here.
No ApoMarioHighscore source or test suite was present in the inspected inventory, so its concrete parser/store/persistence symbols cannot yet be anchored.
The exact player-name source, terminal callback coverage, record eligibility for AI/replay/editor modes, and highscore file format remain unresolved.

Highscore menu view and displayed ordering
B1 local highscore store ingestion
nodes.sink: Highscore record allocation, sorting, getters, and menu rendering
nodes.source: The future ApoMarioHighscore(Path) constructor and persistence reader; analogous local file reads use FileInputStream in ApoMarioConstants.loadProperties()
nodes.untrusted_input: A file at the Path supplied to ApoMarioHighscore, editable by the local user

nodes.label: B2 player-name input
nodes.sink: The name argument of the future storeRun(int,int,String), then persisted storage and menu display

nodes.label: ApoMarioLevel stores a countdown in time, initializes levelStartTime from it, exposes getTime(), and decrements time on every thinkTime(delta) call.
nodes.task_relevance: The feature must derive survival time from level state at the terminal event and normalize it to mm:ss.
nodes.verification: Exercise a run with known deltas and assert recorded elapsed time equals the start countdown minus the terminal countdown, clamped and formatted as mm:ss.

nodes.label: Player points are mutable, reset during ApoMarioPlayer.init(), increased for coins, and adjusted in ApoMarioLevel.setAnalysis(boolean) for win outcomes.
nodes.task_relevance: The record must occur after terminal scoring so the highscore receives the real final score.
nodes.verification: Complete and lose runs, then assert the stored score is the terminal player score and that a run is recorded once per terminal transition.

nodes.label: The menu currently routes start, options, credits, simulation, replay loading, editor loading, and player loading through named functions and node transitions; no highscore function or dedicated highscore panel is present in the inspected menu symbols.
nodes.task_relevance: Highscore display requires a new menu route and panel integration while preserving existing routes.
nodes.verification: Navigate to the new menu item and verify the dedicated view renders all persisted records without changing existing menu transitions.

nodes.label: Existing properties persistence reads mario.properties with FileInputStream and writes it with FileOutputStream, while malformed numeric properties fall back to bounded defaults.
nodes.task_relevance: The highscore store needs an explicit, bounded file format and failure behavior consistent with the desktop persistence model.
nodes.verification: Inspect the chosen highscore file format and test missing, malformed, oversized, and partially written files.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject the invalid record or entire invalid store at the parser boundary and continue with an empty bounded in-memory board so the menu remains available.
nodes.label: A user-editable highscore file could inject malformed or extreme record counts, scores, times, or names, causing uncontrolled allocation, parser failure, corrupted ordering, or unsafe rendering if accepted without validation.
nodes.task_relevance: The new constructor and persistence reader cross the local-file trust boundary B1.
nodes.verification: Feed the store parser negative counts, huge counts, invalid integers, oversized names, invalid times, truncation, and extra data; verify bounded memory and a usable empty/partial board.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject records that fail the chosen integrity/format checks; if authenticity cannot be established, retain only normalized valid records and use a documented untrusted-store status rather than treating them as authoritative.
nodes.label: A locally editable highscore file can tamper with scores, names, and ordering, allowing fabricated rankings; a plain persistence mechanism provides no authenticity guarantee.
nodes.task_relevance: The highscore file is explicitly local and persisted across runs, so its integrity is exposed to the fixed local-cheating threat model at B1.
nodes.verification: Modify persisted scores and names between launches and verify invalid records are rejected or normalized according to the selected integrity policy.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject or normalize invalid name input at the input boundary; at recording/display integration use a bounded fallback such as "Player" so the run is still recorded and displayed.
nodes.label: Unsanitized player names can cause control characters, excessive layout width, or misleading highscore display when passed from text input to persistence and rendering.
nodes.task_relevance: The name crosses B2 and is displayed by the new panel.
nodes.verification: Submit empty, whitespace-only, maximum-length, non-ASCII, control-character, and clipboard names; verify accepted names are bounded and the fallback still creates a record.

nodes.failure_behavior: Record exactly once after final score adjustment and before the level is reset; if score/name/time is invalid at this integration point, substitute bounded normalized defaults and continue the analysis/menu transition.
nodes.label: Recording before terminal scoring or deriving elapsed time from a reset/new level can persist a non-final score or incorrect survival time; repeated callbacks can also duplicate one run.
nodes.task_relevance: The terminal flow currently computes scoring in setAnalysis(boolean), while game/menu transitions can restart or replace the level.
nodes.verification: Instrument terminal win, loss, timeout, replay, editor, restart, and repeated-callback paths; assert one record only for eligible human runs and that the recorded values are terminal values.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject malformed dimensions, counts, coordinates, timer values, and trailing/incomplete records at decoding; at run-end integration use bounded defaults for unavailable elapsed time or name so the highscore effect still occurs.
nodes.label: Network or local level data is decoded into dimensions, timer values, entity counts, coordinates, and allocations without visible bounds in the inspected reader; using such state as the source of a highscore can make malformed shared content influence memory use or recorded results.
nodes.task_relevance: This is the reachable server-content/local-file boundary B3 when a loaded level is later finished and recorded.
nodes.verification: Use crafted local and served level streams with invalid dimensions/counts/coordinates/times and verify decoding rejects them before allocation; verify a valid level still permits run recording.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject invalid records/store data and fall back to an empty or valid bounded board; do not allocate based on an untrusted count.
nodes.label: The highscore store operation that first receives persisted bytes must parse only a bounded, versioned record format; each record must have a bounded normalized name, non-negative bounded score, and non-negative bounded survival time, and records must be sorted by score descending while keeping fields aligned.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects persisted highscore integrity and availability at B1 and satisfies the required getters and ordering.
nodes.verification: Property-test parsing with malformed counts, values, names, truncation, duplicates, and unsorted records; assert bounded allocation, aligned getter lists, and descending scores.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject invalid name characters at the input boundary, then use the stated fallback "Player" at storeRun so the primary record effect occurs.
nodes.label: The name-receiving storeRun operation must accept only a bounded normalized player name and must persist the same normalized value used by the board; empty or invalid names must not prevent recording a run.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects the name-to-store flow at B2 and ensures every completed run still has a displayable name.
nodes.verification: Call storeRun with null, empty, whitespace, control, oversized, and printable names and verify normalization/fallback plus persisted/displayed equality.

nodes.failure_behavior: At the integration point, substitute score 0, normalized fallback name "Player", and elapsed time 0 when a value is missing or invalid, then continue the analysis/menu transition.
nodes.label: The run-end operation must receive the final ApoMarioLevel state only after terminal scoring, record the actual player score, normalized player name, and elapsed survival time, and be idempotent for one run; it must cover both clearing and losing a run.
nodes.task_relevance: Implements the requested recordRunEnd(ApoMarioLevel) behavior at B3 and prevents stale/reset values or duplicate entries.
nodes.verification: Run deterministic win/loss/timeout cases, including repeated terminal calls and replay/editor modes; assert one record per eligible run with final score and elapsed time.

nodes.failure_behavior: On read failure use an empty valid board; on write failure retain the in-memory record and continue to the menu, reporting persistence failure without dropping the run effect.
nodes.label: The persistence operation must write highscore records atomically enough that a partial write cannot become the next run's accepted board, and a read/write failure must not suppress the already completed run or make the menu unavailable.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects persistence across runs and availability of the dedicated menu view at B1/B4.
nodes.verification: Simulate missing, read-only, truncated, and interrupted store files across process restarts; verify no crash, no unbounded retry, and preservation of the in-memory record.

nodes.failure_behavior: If a getter value is unavailable or invalid at display integration, render a bounded fallback label/value and keep the panel navigable.
nodes.label: The menu integration must expose a dedicated highscore panel/view that reads the validated getter data and displays names, descending scores, and mm:ss survival times without allowing untrusted values to control layout or navigation.
nodes.task_relevance: Satisfies the requested dedicated menu display at B4.
nodes.verification: Navigate from the menu, render empty and full boards with long names and boundary times, and verify stable layout, descending order, mm:ss formatting, and back navigation.

nodes.failure_behavior: Skip or reject malformed records and use an empty bounded board if the store structure is invalid.
nodes.label: Implement a bounded parser/decoder at ApoMarioHighscore store ingestion with explicit maximum records/name length/score/time, strict numeric parsing, field-count checks, and record sorting using a single record object so parallel getter lists cannot desynchronize.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R1 at B1 before allocation and display.
nodes.verification: Fuzz and unit-test the constructor/read path with malformed and oversized files, checking allocation and sorted aligned outputs.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject invalid input at entry, then fall back to "Player" in storeRun rather than suppressing the run record.
nodes.label: Enforce name normalization at the name input and storeRun boundaries: trim, reject control characters and excessive length, and replace null/empty/invalid values with "Player" at the recording integration point.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects B2 and ensures a completed run is still stored.
nodes.verification: Test UI, clipboard, direct storeRun, and persisted reload paths with invalid names.

nodes.failure_behavior: Use score 0, "Player", and elapsed time 0 for invalid values, then continue to the existing analysis/editor transition.
nodes.label: Call recordRunEnd(level) once from the terminal scoring path after setAnalysis(boolean) has applied final points and before restart/new-level state is created; guard it with a per-run recorded flag and exclude replay/editor/simulation modes according to the product policy.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces final-value and idempotency requirements for B3.
nodes.verification: Test win, loss, timeout, restart, repeated callback, replay, editor, and simulation paths for exactly-once behavior and final values.

nodes.failure_behavior: Keep the validated in-memory board on write failure and use an empty valid board on read failure; continue the completed run and menu transition.
nodes.label: Write the validated board through a temporary file followed by an atomic replacement where supported, and load into memory before exposing getters; isolate persistence exceptions from menu and run-end control flow.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces persistence continuity and menu availability for B1/B4.
nodes.verification: Inject I/O failures and interrupted writes, restart the application, and assert no partial board is accepted and no run/menu effect is lost.

nodes.failure_behavior: Render fallback values for missing entries and preserve back/menu navigation.
nodes.label: Expose a dedicated panel through ApoMarioPanel initialization and menu routing, and render only bounded validated getter values with fixed-width or clipped name layout and mm:ss formatting.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces safe highscore display and navigation at B4.
nodes.verification: UI-test empty, populated, malformed-recovered, long-name, and boundary-time boards, including keyboard/mouse navigation.

nodes.label: Run unit tests for storeRun, all three getter lists, descending score ordering, survival-time formatting, malformed-store recovery, and persistAcrossRuns using a temporary Path.
nodes.task_relevance: Verifies R1, R2, and R4.
nodes.verification: Create, reload, and compare a temporary store across separate ApoMarioHighscore instances; include malformed and interrupted files.

nodes.label: Run integration tests for recordRunEnd(ApoMarioLevel) on deterministic win and loss levels, asserting actual terminal score, normalized name, elapsed seconds, and exactly-once persistence before reset.
nodes.task_relevance: Verifies R3 and C3.
nodes.verification: Use controlled player points and timer deltas, invoke both terminal outcomes and repeated callbacks, and inspect the resulting store.

nodes.label: Run UI tests from the existing menu event flow into the dedicated highscore view and back, checking descending display order, bounded names, mm:ss output, empty-board behavior, and rendering under malformed-store recovery.
nodes.task_relevance: Verifies R5 and C5.
nodes.verification: Exercise keyboard and mouse routing with empty, normal, long-name, and recovered boards.

nodes.task_relevance: Verifies all previously unknown implementation edges and prevents security context drift.
nodes.verification: Inspect outline.md and code-model.json after implementation and replace provisional/null enforcement anchors with concrete resolved symbols.

nodes.task_relevance: The implementing model must define these operations before the requirements can be checked against concrete enforcement points.

nodes.verification: Trace the final implementation from player-name entry through ApoMarioLevel and storeRun, and verify it does not use the level-seed field as the player name accidentally.

nodes.label: The inspected source does not resolve every terminal event path that causes a run to be considered finished, including the exact loss/timeout callback and whether simulation, editor, and replay completions are eligible for the player highscore.

nodes.verification: Resolve all callers of setAnalysis and all player-death/finish transitions in code-model.json, then execute each path with a run-recording spy.

summary: ApoMario already maintains mutable per-player points and a countdown timer in ApoMarioLevel, updates them during gameplay, and transitions to an analysis view through setAnalysis(boolean). Menu panels are selected through ApoMarioPanel and ApoMarioMenu. Existing persistence is a plain properties file, while levels/replays use local or network-backed binary/text readers. The requested highscore store, player-name source, and end-of-run integration do not yet exist in the inspected sources.
